title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore East on 1970-09-20

ai_review.summary: Remastered soundboard capture of the legendary 9/20/70 Fillmore East show delivers a superb acoustic set and fire‑blazing Easy Wind, with clear but still slightly hissy audio.
ai_review.review: The September 20, 1970 Fillmore East performance is hailed as one of the band’s peak acoustic shows – highlighted by Rosalie McFall, New Speedway, Brokedown Palace and a transcendent To Lay Me Down – and an electric half that erupts on Easy Wind, Not Fade Away→Caution→Feedback→Goodnight and Sugar Magnolia.  The SirMick remaster cleans up much of the original tape hiss and volume wobble, though a faint hiss remains in the acoustic set and the drums are occasionally mixed high.  Overall the music outweighs the minor sonic flaws, making this release a must‑have for Deadheads.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 80% of reviews are five‑star and praise both the performance (standout acoustic set, iconic Easy Wind, strong solos) and the remastered soundboard source.  Minor complaints about residual hiss and occasional mix quirks keep the rating just shy of perfect.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Remaster reduces tape hiss and level fluctuations; some hiss still audible in acoustic set, occasional volume dip on Caution, drums mixed a bit high, occasional warble/drop‑outs but overall clear and listenable.

standout_songs: Not Fade Away > Caution > Feedback > Goodnight
show_quality.setlist_flow: A flawless acoustic first set that showcases the band’s folk‑rock roots, followed by an electric second set that builds momentum through extended jams and culminates in a classic NFA‑Caution‑Feedback sequence; the transition feels natural and captures the 1970 Fillmore East vibe.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar tone described as ‘out of control’, superb on Easy Wind and TLMD; also praised for piano work on To Lay Me Down.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil Lesh’s bass noted as “primo” and a solid low‑end foundation throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bobby (Bob) Weir highlighted for lead guitar fire on Easy Wind, strong solos on Sugar Magnolia and overall ‘on fire’ performance.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ praised on Me and My Uncle and other tracks; keyboards add texture but some reviewers note they are less prominent than the guitars.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming generally solid, though a few reviews mention drums mixed too high in spots.
